title: Tailoring Strictly Proper Scoring Rules for Downstream Tasks: An Application to Causal Inference
claim: The tailored divergence closely tracks the downstream task error near the true value, while the standard divergence badly underestimates it.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, shared legend below, log-y axes, dashed vertical line at truth
description: Two side-by-side line plots with a log-scaled y-axis from 1e-6 to 1e4 and probability q on the x-axis. The left panel has true p=0.01 and x from 0 to 0.05. The right panel has p=0.4 and x from 0 to 1. A gray dashed vertical line marks p in each panel, and its label is rotated. Three curves are drawn in each panel: a solid red task divergence, a dashed blue curve labeled as ours, and a dash-dotted green KL divergence. All curves dip sharply to a minimum at p. In the left panel the blue and red curves overlap almost exactly and sit orders of magnitude above the green curve. In the right panel blue lies slightly above red and both stay well above green. A shared legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the V-shaped dips at the dashed line and to the gap between green and the other two curves.
caption: \textbf{$d_\ell$ locally behaves as $d_{task}$}. Log-scale plots of $q \mapsto d(p,q)$ for $d \in \{d_{task}, d_\ell, d_{\mathrm{KL}}\}$. The vertical dashed lines indicate the true probability $p$, with $p=0.01$ in the left panel and $p=0.4$ in the right panel.
abstract: Probabilistic models are typically trained using task-agnostic objectives like log-loss, which can lead to significant errors in downstream estimation. This disconnect is especially critical in Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) for causal inference, where propensity score errors near $0$ and $1$ often lead to high bias and variance. We propose a principled framework for deriving task-specific strictly proper scoring rules by matching the local curvature of the downstream error metric. We apply this to the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) estimation, deriving a closed-form loss and its corresponding canonical probability mapping that can be readily integrated with any model like a neural network or a gradient boosting algorithm. Extensive evaluations on causal inference benchmarks demonstrate that our tailored objective consistently outperforms standard likelihood-based and covariate-balancing approaches.
